answer.evidence: This is a tile overlay of four leafy crown clumps seen from above on a dark green background. Each clump is a lumpy mass with light highlights at the upper left and darker green at the lower right. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no vertical front face of 3 or more rows; the clumps are shaded only as rounded foliage. The silhouette is a full 48-wide tile with no width profile that shows a cap or a shaft. It reads as a flat top-down canopy texture with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a 64x64 tile of canopy crown heads with about 15 colours in total and a per-tile median of 15, against 108-109 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. That is far below both. It has 0% flat-fill coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the dark outlines are tinted dark green and not black. Shading is roughly 4 green steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep shadow) in rounded clumps. The references have 6+ greens with fine per-leaf clumps, highlight speckle and dithering. The candidate's crown heads are smooth, blobby lumps with only a little speckle, so the texture is simpler and more sticker-like. Because it is much lower in colour count and density, it does not match the reference richness.
